items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I had a Mani Manetta on the piano, and I was playing guitar.

ctx.x: Yeah, that was my job. I had Mani Manetta. Who else did you? I had the old man, Umprey. Willie Umprey, the clarinet player, yeah. And I had a Mani Manetta on the piano, and I was playing guitar. That time I was playing guitar. And John Vino on the drum. And... Let's see, we only had five pieces. See, I count five. Mani Manetta, Willie Umprey, John Vino, myself, and the piano.
Did you have a carnet in those days?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: 1907 at Harry Parker's Dance Hall, Dawson and Minetta's Band, Franklin between Iberville and Benwood.

ctx.x: I'll ask a couple questions, see like where you were born right here in New Orleans.

I started the playing in 1904 at Hugh Cloth's Dance Hall with O'Neill Lavish's Band, Franklin Y. Iberville. 1905 at Tom Anderson with Moran's Band, Basin and Iberville. 1907 at Harry Parker's Dance Hall, Dawson and Minetta's Band, Franklin between Iberville and Benwood. 1910 at Biller Phillips Dance Hall, Cornelius Jackson's Band, Franklin near Iberville. 1912 Liberty near Iberville, Huntson Nagel's Dance Hall with Joe Oliver's Band. 1915 with Chris Kelly's Band. 1918 Kid René's Band. 1921 Pippa Light Charles Band.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I was at Harry Porphy and Charlie Porphy running my own band then. I got with Marion Vanilla, and, uh, had my own line up there.

ctx.x: A little cigarette. And you just played with him, he had two pieces, just guitar and violin. No, we had a bass, too.

Oh, yeah. Yeah. And, uh, from that on, I just kept on going, and I would work myself on up there, you know, when I found myself, I was, I was at Harry Porphy and Charlie Porphy running my own band then. I got with Marion Vanilla, and, uh, had my own line up there.
What did Coochie Martin play when you were playing with him the other day?
